text: The same star schema idea, at a harder version: one fact table, one fixed grain — one row per order line — surrounded by dimensions built from the crosswalk, not copied from either source directly.
DimCustomer comes from the CRM through the crosswalk. DimProduct comes from the inventory system's SKUs. Every foreign key in FactOrders points at a conformed key, never a raw source identifier.
Customers load first, inventory in parallel, orders last — because writing an order-line row requires a valid customer_key and product_key that only exist once the crosswalk has resolved them.
The nightly reconciliation query now has something real to check: FactOrders' totals against the legacy system's totals, every night — the first real signal this warehouse is trustworthy.
A target warehouse built on conformed keys, loaded in the order the dependencies demand. Next up: planning the actual cutover strategy.
